expected_differences.observed_legacy_behavior: a RAPID profile value satisfies a rule group written for ULTRARAPID, because PROFILE_MATCH_GROUPS['rapid'] contains 'ultrarapid'
expected_differences.required_v2_behavior: NO_MATCH. A rule covering both phenotypes must declare both in a ONE_OF set
expected_differences.safety_rationale: implicit equivalence applies a rule outside the evidence it was written from, which is an unreviewed scientific claim

expected_differences.observed_legacy_behavior: an ULTRARAPID profile value satisfies a rule group written for RAPID, because PROFILE_MATCH_GROUPS['ultrarapid'] contains 'rapid'
expected_differences.required_v2_behavior: NO_MATCH. The reverse direction is a separate entry because the legacy table states it separately, and a fix that closed only one direction would satisfy a single-entry allowlist
expected_differences.safety_rationale: same defect, opposite direction; both must be closed or a rule still fires for a phenotype nobody reviewed it against

expected_differences.observed_legacy_behavior: PROFILE_MATCH_GROUPS['normal'] is the empty set, so a NORMAL profile value satisfies no rule at all - including a rule written for NORMAL
expected_differences.required_v2_behavior: MATCH. NORMAL equals NORMAL; whether a matched rule warrants any attention is carried by the rule's own outcome, which may be NO_ACTIVE_ATTENTION, and is decided downstream
expected_differences.safety_rationale: the legacy table answers 'should this raise a flag?' inside a function that is asked 'is this the same phenotype?'. Suppressing the match makes an evaluated rule indistinguishable from an axis no rule covered, which is the false-reassurance failure SAFETY-INV-001 exists to prevent. V2 separates the two: equality here, attention in WP-14

expected_differences.observed_legacy_behavior: POOR and INTERMEDIATE both satisfy a rule group written for the invented group 'decreased_function', and a supplied value containing 'decreased' becomes that group
expected_differences.required_v2_behavior: 'decreased_function' is not a phenotype and is not a rule vocabulary member: as an input it is UNSUPPORTED, and no condition can declare it
expected_differences.safety_rationale: the P0 phenotype model has six members and this is not one of them; expanding a broad functional group into POOR or INTERMEDIATE invents a mapping no curator made

note: This report compares phenotype normalisation and matcher semantics only. It compares no clinical output, because no approved ruleset exists to produce one. A difference listed here is a difference in how a value is read or compared, never a statement about any medicine.
